qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Owns 2.7 million hectares of forest land in northern Sweden, representing irreplaceable European forestry infrastructure and low-cost self-sufficient fiber supply. However, end-market products (NBSK pulp, kraftliner, sawn timber) are global price-taking commodities with zero pricing power. Group ROCE averages 3-7% (failing 12% hurdle), burdened by heavy mill reinvestment capex.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing). Europe's largest private forest owner with world-class integrated mills, but commodity price-taking outputs (pulp, kraftliner, wood) and massive capital base result in multi-cycle Group ROCE of 3-6%, well below the 12% threshold.
qualitative.evidence: Reported Group ROCE was 6.9% in 2019, 3.4% in 2020, 5.4% in 2021, 4.0% in 2022, 3.3% in 2023, and 4.4% in 2024. Even Industrial ROCE dropped back to 7.3% in 2023-2024 following the 2021-2022 cyclical pulp price spike. Multi-cycle Group ROIC fails the 12% standard, and large-scale mill capex (Östrand, Obbola) absorbs substantial cash flow.
